life_summary: John Henry Smith was born September 19, 1848, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory, to apostle George A. Smith. He grew to manhood in a prominent church family, inheriting both spiritual responsibility and civic engagement. Smith received education appropriate to his station and participated in the early development of Utah Territory. He married and fathered nineteen children through plural marriage, establishing a large and influential family. Smith was known for his integrity and his ability to bridge ecclesiastical and political spheres. He died of pulmonary hemorrhage in Salt Lake City, having witnessed and participated in many of the transformative events of Utah's territorial period.
church_summary: John Henry Smith held various positions within the LDS Church beginning in 1867. He served as a European missionary in 1874–1875, primarily in England, spreading Church influence during a significant period of international expansion. In October 1880, Church president John Taylor called Smith to be a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. Following the death of John R. Winder, he joined the First Presidency in 1910, serving as counselor to the Church president. Smith served alongside his father George A. Smith in the Quorum of the Twelve from 1903 to 1910, making them one of the few father-son pairs to serve together in that governing body.
